:::note[Written against main]
This page follows `main` at c118b2f, and it differs from the copy in HotLoop core 4.18.10, the latest release. Parts of it may be newer than what you have installed. The [release notes](/releases/) say what moved.
:::

The release where HotLoop stops being one image. IoT, Edge, the Gateway and the
Edge Relay all ship from this tag, in lockstep, each with its own image and its
own chart. On top of that: devices that announce themselves over MQTT, history
written out to the plant's own database, a database you pick (SQLite, Postgres
or TimescaleDB), an Edge that keeps working with the WAN dead, and boxes that
follow `:stable` and roll a bad update back on their own. Coming from 4.17.0 the
Gateway is a plain `helm upgrade`. Read "Upgrading from 4.17.0" below before you
touch a running plant, because a couple of defaults moved.

There is no 4.18.0, 4.18.1, 4.18.2, 4.18.3, 4.18.4, 4.18.5, 4.18.6, 4.18.7 or 4.18.9 to install, and 4.18.8
is not one to run. I tagged all ten. Nine of them published nothing, no image, no
chart and no release. 4.18.8 passed every test and then I cancelled its run by
mistake while it was publishing, so it left images on ghcr.io with no chart and no
release (more on that below). The first three
died in the Test job. CI ran Docker on a small shared runner and my lab runs
Podman on a big box, and the integration services' script had three things only
the lab forgave. The network-discovery image was built without naming its
Containerfile. InfluxDB 3's token file went in readable by root alone, which
Docker leaves it as and Podman quietly hands to the container's user. SQL Server
died at boot when the runner was busy starting everything else, so it starts on
its own first now and gets tried again if it dies. The port 465 test had no
relay to run against, so it skipped, and a skip fails the release. Two reloads
of the runtime at once could race on a worker, and reloads take turns now. The
fourth, 4.18.3, got past all of that, started every service, and ran the runner
out of disk five minutes into the tests: a hosted runner starts a job with 14 GB
free, the service images are 10.5 GB of it, and Go took the rest. The job clears
the toolchains it never uses before it pulls anything now, and prints where the
disk went whether it passes or not. The fifth, 4.18.4, had the room and died in
the Test job anyway, on two tests that only fail on a starved box: a test broker
that counted a client which had already hung up, and a browser test that builds
a dashboard. So the rehearsal of the release stopped being a quiet box. The Test
job runs on two CPUs, the runner's RAM and the runner's disk, with something
else burning CPU beside it, and a release isn't tagged until that has
passed. What it turned up is fixed here: a discovered device's
value could be stamped older than its own "nothing yet" reading and the cache
dropped it, which is a bug in the product and not in the test, the dashboard
stops redrawing a gauge that hasn't changed, and the test Chrome runs without
its GPU, because software GL was eating both CPUs. And the images and charts are
built with Podman and Buildah now, where the release workflow and the test
services still talked to a Docker engine. `Dockerfile` and
`Dockerfile.edge-relay` are `Containerfile` and `Containerfile.edge-relay`. The sixth,
4.18.5, passed all of that here and died on the runner before a single test
ran: the suite mounts Go's module cache from the runner's home directory, a
fresh runner doesn't have that directory yet, and Podman won't mount a folder
that isn't there where Docker quietly made one. The suite makes it first now. The seventh,
4.18.6, ran every test and lost one: ntfy refused an alarm notification that
carried the right token. That's a race inside ntfy itself. It files a request
under its sender's address and briefly forgets who the sender is while it
checks a password, so a token publish that lands beside a password request from
the same address reads as nobody, and the lockdown turns it away. HotLoop sent
the right thing. The test ntfy gives its user its own lane now, and if your
phones log in to ntfy with a password from the same address HotLoop publishes
from, give that user a tier too. The eighth,
4.18.7, lost the one test that had been flaky all week, and it was a real bug.
The broker built into HotLoop checked a client's SUBSCRIBE packet id against
the messages it was sending that same client. MQTT numbers those two apart and
both start at 1, so a listener that subscribed while it was being sent QoS 1
traffic got refused, the client library called the refusal a grant, and the
device behind that subscription was never discovered. The check is gone, a
raw packet test proves it, and a broker that refuses a subscription is logged
now instead of shrugged off. The ninth,
4.18.8, passed every test. I cancelled its run by hand, because the same broker
had the mirror image of that bug and I wanted both fixes in one release, and I
thought it was still testing. It wasn't. It was publishing. By then the Gateway,
Edge Relay, IoT and Edge images were already pushed as 4.18.8, and the Gateway,
Edge Relay and IoT ones had moved `:stable` and `:latest` with them. No chart and
no release followed, and 4.18.10 replaces it, so a box that follows `:stable` may
have run 4.18.8 until it updated. The mirror image was this: when a client
published with the same packet
id as a QoS 1 or 2 message the broker still owed it, the broker threw its own
message away and never resent it after a reconnect. The broker keeps the two
directions in separate tables now, with a test for each QoS, and that fix is
in this release. The tenth,
4.18.9, lost one browser test to a real bug: a dashboard still loading wrote
its address over the one the person had just moved to, so a reload put them
back on the dashboard they had left. A dashboard only takes the address now if
nobody has moved it since it started loading. 4.18.10
is everything 4.18.0 was going to be, plus what changed on main since 4.18.3 was
tagged.

The full notes are in the README:
What changed in 4.18.10.

## In short

- **Built with Podman.** The images and the charts come out of Podman and Buildah,
  and `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.edge-relay` are `Containerfile` and
  `Containerfile.edge-relay`. Same four images, same tags, same architectures.
- **Since 4.18.4 was tagged.** A discovered device's value could be lost behind its
  own "nothing yet" reading and is not now. A UPnP device whose description
  failed to read is read again in seconds, not after 15 minutes. OK on the card
  editor works on the first click, Save in the entity drawer stays put, the dashboard stops redrawing
  what hasn't changed, and a counter two processes hammer no longer refuses the
  one that keeps losing.
- **The license changed.** All four products are under HotLoop's Business
  Source License 1.1 now. Home and lab use is free, so is use by schools,
  nonprofits and government, and business use goes through EmberNET. Each
  version turns into GPL-3.0 or later four years after it first goes out.
  It is not open source until then, and I'm not going to pretend it is.
  Read LICENSE
  before you put it on a plant.
- **Since 4.18.3 was tagged.** UniFi on a wall board and a phone: the network
  map zooms and pinches, WAN latency and port traffic get traces, and one button
  makes the usual alarms. An agent can ask over MCP for the network's map
  (`get_network_topology`) and what the console just said (`get_network_events`).
  The logbook shows UniFi events under the switch they are about. One MQTT device
  could get two clients with the same id, and the broker kicked each in turn;
  that is fixed. Alarm messages print a value the way the value card does, the
  alarms card can be pointed at devices or equipment, and a trend of a tag that
  holds still is a line across the window.
- **Four products, four images, four charts, one tag.** `hotloop-iot` and
  `hotloop-edge` are new on ghcr.io and in the chart repository. The Gateway
  keeps `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop` and the chart `hotloop`, so nobody running
  it changes anything. A product is a build, not a setting: the OPC UA server
  isn't switched off in the IoT image, it isn't in it. See
  docs/PRODUCTS.md.
- **MQTT discovery.** Point ESPHome, Zigbee2MQTT, Tasmota or a Shelly at the
  broker and it shows up, reading. It can't command anything until an admin
  accepts it and arms each point by hand. Network discovery (mDNS, SSDP, DHCP)
  listens and sends nothing unless you list a network to probe.
- **Historian targets.** Every reading HotLoop keeps also goes to the plant's
  own PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, SQL Server, InfluxDB or MySQL/MariaDB, the same
  rows with the same quality.
- **The database is a setting.** SQLite, PostgreSQL or TimescaleDB per product,
  from the same binary. A Pi doesn't need a 300 MB database image.
- **Edge keeps the plant running with the WAN dead,** and its store and forward
  queue survives the ugly cases: a boot during an outage, a link that dies
  without a reset, a replay that has to outrun the plant.
- **Every box follows `:stable` and updates itself,** and a release that can't
  start is rolled back. Migrations only add, and an app refuses to start on a
  schema two releases ahead of it, so that rollback is always safe.
- **The Edge Relay** takes a pushed config live, with no restart and no lost
  Sparkplug session, and discovers devices on a broker like the Gateway does.
- **Every image carries every third-party license,** and a GPL module stops the
  build.
- **The sun.** Sunrise, sunset and the sun's height, worked out on the box from
  a latitude and a longitude.

### API changes

- New routes: `/api/discovery`, `/api/network-discovery`, `/api/mqtt/brokers`,
  `/api/broker/logins`, `/api/historian/targets`,
  `GET /api/entities/{entity_id}/image` and `POST /api/fleet/{id}/update`. All
  in docs/API.md.
- `GET /api/status` says `product` and `features`, and the image digest. A route
  for a feature the product you're talking to doesn't have answers `404` with
  the product that does, instead of pretending. Every route is still there in
  every product.
- New permission `fleet.update`, admin only. The operator role didn't change.

### Upgrading from 4.17.0

- `helm upgrade <release> hotloop/hotloop --version 4.18.10
  --reset-then-reuse-values`. I rendered the 4.17.0 and 4.18.10 Gateway charts
  side by side: the same eight objects, the same selectors, the same volume
  claims. Plain `--reuse-values` renders too this time, but it replays 4.17.0's
  values and drops every new default, so use the reset form or your values file.
- Migrations 0016 to 0024 run on start (MQTT discovery, broker logins, MQTT
  sources, historian targets, network finds, two more for what the MQTT sources
  speak, the table dashboards are saved in, and a `no_data` column on tags that
  is empty for every tag that already exists).
  All additive. `pg_dump` first, like always.
- **`edgePublish.queueMaxBytes` defaults to 64 MiB now, not unbounded.** Past
  it the oldest readings are dropped and counted. An unbounded queue filled the
  volume in a long outage, which is worse, but it is a changed default: size it
  from your own reading rate (about 180 bytes a reading) or set it to `0` to
  keep the old behavior. An upgrade with `--reuse-values` keeps whatever you
  had.
- **Broker logins.** Logins you make in Settings, MQTT carry topic rules from a
  profile. Logins from `HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS` are untouched and can do anything,
  exactly as before. A broker with no `HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS` starts now, and only
  HotLoop and the logins made in it get in.
- **Going back to 4.17.0** works: the schema only grew, and 4.17.0 runs on it.
  `test/prevrelease.sh` proves that against the published 4.17.0 image before
  every release. From here on the app also counts how far ahead its database is
  and refuses by name at two releases, so a rollback is never a surprise.
- **Edge Relay:** upgrade it with `--reset-then-reuse-values` too. Quadlet users
  take the new `edge-relay.container`, which follows `:stable` instead of
  pinning 4.17.0, and the healthcheck that makes a bad update roll back.
- **Quadlet units for IoT, Edge and the Gateway are new.** 4.17.0 only had the
  relay's. They are under `deploy/quadlet/`, one directory per product.

### What isn't proven

- **Edge and IoT as live Quadlet units under systemd,** except IoT's SQLite
  unit, which was run. The rest are generated from the Gateway's, checked
  against them, and not started. The Gateway's units were run for real,
  rootless under systemd, including an update that migrates and then can't
  start and gets rolled back. A real Pi under systemd as root: not yet.
- **Moving a site up a product as a `helm upgrade` on a real cluster,** and going
  back down one. The Quadlet move, IoT to Edge to Gateway on one database
  volume, has been run.
- **Discovery against real devices is proven against recordings** of real
  installs, not against devices on a bench here. ESPHome's `mqtt:` component
  doesn't build for a host, so there is no live ESPHome in CI.
- **The 32-bit arm images on real hardware.** A Pi 3 under load: not yet.
